subject: Consolidate sandbox stipend with deferred committed discount — coordination request
messages:
From: Sophie Tran <sophie@launchlabs.io>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: Samir Kohli <samir@seedfoundry.vc>
Date: 2029-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Sandbox stipend + pilot path question

Hi Diego —

Thanks again for the demo last week. LaunchLabs is excited to run a 6-week sandbox with a small cohort of teams. Two quick asks before we finalize: 

1) Can the $15k sandbox stipend be applied against a paid committed tier if we convert to Dedicated within 90 days?
2) If we do a convert-and-commit, can we get a staged discount (e.g., 20% first 3 months, 10% months 4-12) rather than a one-time credit?

Attached is a rough usage estimate to help pricing (LaunchLabs_Usage_Estimate.xlsx). We also have a legal playbook that prefers credits to be true discounts rather than marketing stipend offsets for tax reasons.

Can you confirm next steps and what paperwork Finance/Legal will need?

Best,
Sophie
Head of Partnerships — LaunchLabs
(attachment: LaunchLabs_Usage_Estimate.xlsx)

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: Sophie Tran <sophie@launchlabs.io>
Cc: Samir Kohli <samir@seedfoundry.vc>
Date: 2029-11-01T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sandbox stipend + pilot path question

Hi Sophie —

Really glad LaunchLabs liked the demo. Short answers up front:
- We can make the stipend convertible into a bill credit against a committed contract, but there are two paths (simple offset vs. staged discount) and they have different internal approvals.
- Staged discounts are possible, but Finance will want a clear commitment window and revenue recognition approach — usually that means a documented addendum to the MSAs and a short invoice schedule.

I looped in Laura (Sales Ops) and Irene (Legal) to map the least-friction path. Ben from Finance is on cc for a quick sanity check.

Proposed next step: Laura and I will draft a one-page mutual action plan that shows: conversion window, treatment of the $15k stipend (credit vs. discount), staged discount tiers, and DocuSign-ready signature lines. If that works I’ll attach the sandbox terms and a draft addendum for Legal to review (Sandbox_Terms_v2.pdf).

Expect a first draft by Tuesday EOD.

— Diego
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
(attachment: Sandbox_Terms_v2.pdf)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai; Sophie Tran <sophie@launchlabs.io>, Samir Kohli <samir@seedfoundry.vc>
Date: 2029-11-02T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Draft MAP & conversion choices (for Legal/Finance)

Diego / Irene / Ben —

I put together a short MAP to present two options to LaunchLabs: 

Option A — Stipend as upfront bill credit:
- $15,000 applied as immediate credit at first invoice after conversion.
- Gives LaunchLabs certainty and simpler rev rec.
- Redwood recognizes revenue on normal schedule; credit applied on invoiced amount.

Option B — Stipend converted into staged discounts:
- $15,000 converted into a discount pool which is amortized across first 12 months post-conversion.
- Suggested tiering: 20% discount months 1–3 (up to $8k), 10% months 4–12 (remainder).
- Requires explicit accounting addendum; Finance will need to confirm treatment for ASC/IFRS.

Questions for Legal/Finance:
- Irene: do we need a special contract clause to treat the stipend as a rebate vs. marketing credit to keep tax clean?
- Ben: what documentation does Finance need to support staged discount amortization?

Sophie & Samir — please flag any launch-specific constraints. If you prefer, we can present option language in a single DocuSign packet so your counsel can review one package.

Thanks,
Laura
Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Sophie Tran <sophie@launchlabs.io>
Date: 2029-11-03T11:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP & conversion choices (for Legal/Finance)

Team —

High level: both options are workable, but each has tradeoffs. Notes below for drafting: 

Option A (bill credit)
- Pros: simplest, fast to approve, minimal accounting overhead.
- Cons: if credit exceeds early consumption there are edge cases on refund/rollover we should close.

Option B (staged discount)
- Pros: cleaner match to pricing; reduces sticker shock on month 1.
- Cons: requires the addendum to specify amortization schedule and what happens if customer upgrades/downgrades mid-amortization. Finance must sign-off.

Required clauses for either path:
- Conversion trigger: explicit clause that conversion occurs on signed commitment and start date of paid service.
- Non-transferability: stipend/discount not transferable unless explicitly agreed.
- Termination/upgrade carveouts: define remaining discount pool behavior on early termination or on upgrade to Dedicated.

Ben — please confirm the required accounting memo items; Laura, I can draft addendum language once Ben confirms the fields. Sophie — can you share whether LaunchLabs counsel prefers credits or discounts in principle? If they prefer credits for tax simplicity we’ll push Option A as default.

— Irene
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: Sophie Tran <sophie@launchlabs.io>, Samir Kohli <samir@seedfoundry.vc>
Date: 2029-11-05T16:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP & conversion choices (for Legal/Finance)

Quick finance check —

We can support either option, but prefer Option A (bill credit) from an ops and rev-rec standpoint. If LaunchLabs insists on Option B (staged discount) we’ll need the following documented before the contract is routed for signature:
- Expected monthly usage profile (we can use the attached estimate but need ranges per month).
- A table showing how the $15k maps to discounts at projected usage (so we can model cash impact).
- Statement of treatment in the accounting memo: whether discount is contra-revenue or separate rebate line.

If Sophie confirms that LaunchLabs counsel wants discounts for commercial reasons, Laura and I will prepare the accounting memo and a standard addendum template. Otherwise, we’ll draft the DocuSign packet for Option A and loop in procurement for a quick signature.

Ben
Finance — Redwood Inference
(attachment: Sandbox_Terms_v2.pdf, LaunchLabs_Usage_Estimate.xlsx)
